massachusetts.agency_name: Registry of Vital Records and Statistics, Massachusetts Department of Public Health
massachusetts.birth_certificate: Apply to the Registry of Vital Records and Statistics (Massachusetts Department of Public Health), or to the clerk of the city or town where the birth occurred, with the Applicant Affidavit in Support of Amendment of a Birth Certificate for Sex (form R116), signed under penalty of perjury; if mailed, the affidavit must be notarized. No medical documentation, court order, or proof of a name change is required for the marker change; a certified copy of a legal name-change decree is only needed if you are also changing your name. Fee: $50 one-time amendment fee, plus $32 per certified copy by mail ($20 in person).
massachusetts.court_order_required: No — no court order is required to change the gender marker on either a birth certificate or a driver's license; a court order is needed only if you are also changing your legal name.
massachusetts.drivers_license: Apply in person at a Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) Service Center with a new License/ID Card Application indicating the correct gender marker (M, F, or X). No documentation is required for the gender designation under M.G.L. c. 90, § 8N, and the X marker has been available on licenses and state IDs since November 2019. A name change requires first updating Social Security and bringing a certified copy of the court-ordered name change.
massachusetts.marker_overview: Massachusetts lets you change the gender marker on both a birth certificate and a driver's license or state ID by self-attestation, with M, F, or X available on both documents. No court order, doctor's letter, or surgery is required for the marker itself; a court order is only needed if you are also changing your legal name. A July 2024 law (M.G.L. c. 46, § 13(e) and c. 90, § 8N) streamlined the birth-certificate process and added the X option to birth records.
massachusetts.surgery_required: No — no surgery, medical procedure, or doctor's letter is required for either document; the statute expressly bars officials from requiring any medical or health-care documentation for a marker change.

michigan.agency_name: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS), Vital Records
michigan.birth_certificate: Mail the Application to Correct or Change a Michigan Birth Record and the State of Michigan Sex Designation Form, plus a photocopy of a photo ID, to MDHHS Vital Records. No medical documentation, physician's signature, court order, or surgery is required for the marker change. Fee: $50, which includes one certified copy of the amended certificate; extra copies are $16 each, and optional rush processing (2–3 weeks instead of about 6 weeks) costs an extra $25.
michigan.court_order_required: No — no court order is required to change the gender marker on either a birth certificate or a driver's license; a court order is needed only if you are also changing your legal name.
michigan.drivers_license: Complete the Michigan Secretary of State Sex Designation Form and bring it with your current license or ID to a Secretary of State office in person; you select M, F, or X by self-attestation. No medical documentation, court order, or birth-certificate change is required. Fee: $9 to correct a driver's license, $10 for a state ID; a new photo is taken and the new card is mailed within about two to three weeks.
michigan.marker_overview: Michigan lets you change the gender marker on both a birth certificate and a driver's license or state ID by self-attestation, with M, F, or X available on both documents. No court order, medical documentation, or surgery is required for the marker itself; a court order is only needed if you are also changing your legal name. The birth-certificate change is an administrative amendment through the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS), and the license change is done in person at a Secretary of State office.
michigan.surgery_required: No — no surgery, medical treatment, or doctor's letter is required for either document; both the birth-certificate and license forms are self-attestation only.

minnesota.agency_name: Minnesota Department of Health, Office of Vital Records
minnesota.birth_certificate: Submit a Birth Record Amendment Request to the MDH Office of Vital Records, indicating 'sex' as the item to amend, with either an original letter from a licensed physician certifying appropriate clinical treatment for gender transition or a certified copy of a court order specifically directing amendment of the sex on the birth record. The request must be signed in front of a notary. Fee: $40 amendment fee plus $26 for a certificate with the amended information. Note: if the change is made by amendment without a court order, later certificates note that data items were amended; a court order directing MDH to replace the record seals the original instead. MDH does not publish an X option for birth records.
minnesota.court_order_required: Yes — for a birth certificate only, and only if you do not provide a physician's letter certifying appropriate clinical treatment; a driver's license or state ID never requires a court order.
minnesota.drivers_license: Minnesota Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) lets you choose M, F, or X on a driver's license or state ID by self-designation — it works like changing the eye-color field, with no medical documentation, court order, or extra form required. Just indicate your preferred marker when you apply for or renew your license or ID.
minnesota.marker_overview: Minnesota splits the rules by document: a driver's license or state ID can be changed to M, F, or X by self-designation with no medical documentation or court order, but a birth certificate requires either a physician's letter certifying appropriate clinical treatment for gender transition or a court order directing the change. The birth-certificate change goes through the Minnesota Department of Health (MDH) Office of Vital Records. A 2026 bill (S.F. 5300) that would allow birth-record marker changes by sworn statement has only been introduced, not passed.
minnesota.surgery_required: No — no surgery or medical procedure is required for either document; the birth-certificate physician's letter certifies appropriate clinical treatment for gender transition, which is not a surgery requirement, and no medical proof of any kind is needed for a driver's license.

mississippi.agency_name: Mississippi State Department of Health, Office of Vital Records
mississippi.birth_certificate: Apply to the Mississippi State Department of Health, Office of Vital Records, with Form 1126 (Affidavit to Amend Mississippi Birth Certificate), a certified copy of a court order for change of gender marker, and a physician's letter (medical statement attesting to the reassignment). The change is recorded only as a marginal notation on the original certificate — no new certificate is issued — and only M and F markers are available. Fee: $28, which includes one certified copy; additional copies are $6 each.
mississippi.court_order_required: Yes — a certified court order (plus a medical statement) is required for the birth-certificate marginal notation; for a driver's license, even a court order cannot change the marker after July 1, 2026.
mississippi.drivers_license: As of July 1, 2026, the Mississippi Department of Public Safety must issue every new, renewal, or duplicate driver's license, temporary permit, or commercial license with a sex designation consistent with the sex determined at birth (SB 2322, Miss. Code Ann. § 63-1-35(7)). The designation cannot be changed to reflect gender identity, and a court order inconsistent with this rule has no effect on license issuance or renewal. The only permitted changes are corrections of a scrivener's error, a sex misidentified at birth due to a verifiable disorder of sex development, or a license previously altered to record a sex other than the sex at birth. No X marker is available.
mississippi.marker_overview: Mississippi is now one of the most restrictive states for gender marker changes. Since July 1, 2026, under SB 2322 (Miss. Code Ann. § 63-1-35(7)), every new, renewal, or duplicate driver's license or state ID must show the sex determined at birth, and a court order cannot override that — only a scrivener's error, a verifiable disorder of sex development, or a correction of a license previously altered away from the birth sex can change it. A birth certificate can still record a sex change, but only as a marginal notation (no new certificate is issued), and only with a certified court order plus a medical statement attesting to the reassignment. There is no X option on any Mississippi document.
mississippi.surgery_required: Yes — for a birth certificate, the state requires a physician's letter (medical statement attesting to the reassignment) in addition to a court order; for a driver's license, the marker cannot be changed to reflect gender identity at all after July 1, 2026, regardless of medical evidence.

missouri.agency_name: Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services, Bureau of Vital Records
missouri.birth_certificate: Obtain a certified copy of a court order from a court of competent jurisdiction indicating that the sex of the person born in Missouri has been changed by surgical procedure and that the person's name has been changed (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 193.215(9)), then mail it with a signed cover letter requesting the order be applied to the record to the Bureau of Vital Records, Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services, in Jefferson City. Fee: $15 processing fee, plus $15 per certified copy of the amended certificate.
missouri.court_order_required: Yes — a court order is required for a birth certificate, and for a driver's license it is one of the two accepted routes (the other being proof of gender-affirming surgery).
missouri.drivers_license: Apply in person at a Missouri Department of Revenue license office with either a certified court order declaring the new gender designation or a signed letter from a surgeon confirming gender-affirming surgery. This replaced the pre-August 2024 process, under which a form signed by a physician, therapist, or social worker was enough. Only M and F markers are offered; there is no X option, and the change cannot be done online or by mail.
missouri.marker_overview: Missouri is restrictive and became more so in August 2024, when the Department of Revenue ended its physician-form process for driver's licenses. A birth-certificate change requires a court order stating the sex was changed by surgical procedure (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 193.215(9)), and a driver's license change now requires either a court order or proof of gender-affirming surgery. There is no X marker option, and no standard court form exists for a gender-marker petition, so the court step usually requires a custom petition.
missouri.surgery_required: Yes — the birth-certificate statute requires a court order stating the sex was changed by surgical procedure, and a driver's license change requires either such a court order or documented proof of gender-affirming surgery.

montana.agency_name: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services, Office of Vital Records
montana.birth_certificate: While the injunction is in effect, apply to the DPHHS Office of Vital Records under the restored 2017 rule with an Affidavit for Correction of a Vital Record and the department's Gender Designation Form (your own certification of gender transition or an intersex condition), or with a government-issued ID showing the correct gender, or a certified court order. No court order, medical documentation, or surgery is required while the injunction stands. Fee: $41, which includes one certified copy; additional copies are $16 each. Caution: the underlying ban (SB 280, the 2022 DPHHS rule, and SB 458) remains on the books and could take effect again if the injunction is lifted, since the case is still pending on the merits.
montana.court_order_required: No — no court order is required for a birth certificate while the injunction is in effect; for a driver's license, a court order is one accepted route, but an amended birth certificate works instead.
montana.drivers_license: Apply in person at a Montana Motor Vehicle Division (MVD) office with an amended birth certificate showing your preferred gender or a certified copy of a court order for change of gender, plus proof of identity, your current license or ID, and updated Social Security information. The MVD policy that blocked these changes is also covered by the preliminary injunction affirmed in April 2026. Only M and F markers are available; Montana offers no X option on driver's licenses or state IDs.
montana.marker_overview: Montana's gender-marker rules are currently set by litigation, not by the text printed in the code. The state enacted a 2021 law (SB 280) requiring surgery plus a court order for birth-certificate changes, then a 2022 Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS) rule banning such changes outright, and a Motor Vehicle Division (MVD) policy blocking license changes — but a preliminary injunction against all of those policies was affirmed by the Montana Supreme Court on April 14, 2026 (Kalarchik v. State, 2026 MT 76), so while the injunction is in effect, birth certificates can be changed by affidavit with no surgery or court order, and licenses can be changed with an amended birth certificate or court order. Only M and F markers are issued; X availability is still in litigation.
montana.surgery_required: No — no surgery, medical procedure, or doctor's letter is required while the injunction is in effect; note, however, that the state's blocked 2021 law (SB 280) would require surgery plus a court order if the injunction were lifted.

nebraska.agency_name: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services, Vital Records
nebraska.birth_certificate: Submit an Application for Amendment to the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services, Vital Records, with a notarized affidavit from the physician who performed sex reassignment surgery (stating the surgery and its date) and a certified copy of a court order changing the person's name, as required by Neb. Rev. Stat. § 71-604.01. A new birth certificate is issued and the original is sealed. Fee: $16 amendment fee plus $17 per certified copy.
nebraska.court_order_required: Yes — a court order changing the name is required as part of a birth-certificate change (alongside the surgeon's affidavit); no court order is needed for a driver's license, which uses the provider-signed certification form instead.
nebraska.drivers_license: Apply in person at any Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles driver licensing office (this cannot be done online) with acceptable proof of identification, a completed Certification of Sex Reassignment form signed by a Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Osteopathy, Physician Assistant, Advanced Practice Nurse, or Doctor of Chiropractic certifying that you have undergone the procedures required for social gender recognition, plus a completed license data form and two proofs of address if your address is unverified. Only F or M markers are available; Nebraska offers no X option on driver's licenses or state IDs.
nebraska.marker_overview: Nebraska is restrictive: a birth-certificate change requires both a notarized affidavit from the physician who performed sex reassignment surgery and a court order changing the person's name (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 71-604.01). A driver's license change is somewhat easier — it needs a Certification of Sex Reassignment form signed by a medical provider certifying procedures required for social gender recognition, with no proof of surgery demanded by the DMV form itself — but there is no X option on any Nebraska document, and a 2023 governor's executive order defines gender by reproductive function for state documents.
nebraska.surgery_required: Yes — a birth-certificate change requires a notarized affidavit from the physician who performed sex reassignment surgery; a driver's license requires a medical provider's certification of procedures required for social gender recognition, though the DMV form itself does not demand proof of surgery.

nevada.agency_name: Nevada Division of Public and Behavioral Health, Office of Vital Records and Statistics
nevada.birth_certificate: Mail an Application for a Correction of Birth Record, a notarized Affidavit for Correction of a Record, and a Supplemental Affidavit completed by someone with personal knowledge that you identify as the requested gender (or, instead of the Supplemental Affidavit, a written statement on letterhead from a licensed health-care professional or a court order confirming the change) to the Nevada Office of Vital Records and Statistics, with a copy of the original birth certificate if available. A certified court order is only needed if you are also changing your name. Fee: $40, which includes one certified copy of the amended certificate; additional copies are $20 each.
nevada.court_order_required: No — no court order is required to change the gender marker on either a birth certificate or a driver's license; a court order is needed only if you are also changing your legal name.
nevada.drivers_license: At a Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles office, simply indicate your preferred gender designation (M, F, or X) on the application for a new license or ID. No medical documentation or certification is needed, and Nevada does not require the gender on your license to match the gender on your other documents. A name change requires a certified court order and an updated Social Security record first.
nevada.marker_overview: Nevada makes gender marker changes relatively simple on both documents, with M, F, or X available on each. A birth certificate is changed with notarized affidavits — no court order, medical documentation, or surgery is required — and a driver's license marker is changed by simply selecting your preferred designation on the application, with no medical certification at all. A name change is a separate court process, but the gender marker can be changed on its own.
nevada.surgery_required: No — no surgery, medical procedure, or doctor's letter is required for either document; the birth-certificate Supplemental Affidavit can be completed by any person who knows you, not a medical professional.

new-hampshire.agency_name: New Hampshire Secretary of State, Division of Vital Records Administration
new-hampshire.birth_certificate: Apply to the clerk of the city or town where the birth occurred with Form VSCr (Application for Correcting or Completing a Certificate of Birth), a certified copy of a court order advising that the person has had a sex change (RSA 5-C:87(V)), and a photocopy of a valid photo ID; the clerk then prepares a new birth record reflecting the change. The court order does not require proof of surgery, but what a court will order can vary by judge, and X is not recognized on birth certificates. Fee: $10 amendment fee plus $15 per certified copy.
new-hampshire.court_order_required: Yes — a court order is required for a birth-certificate change only; no court order is needed for a driver's license or state ID.
new-hampshire.drivers_license: At a New Hampshire Division of Motor Vehicles office, choose F, M, or X on the license or ID application (form DSMV 450 for a gender-marker update). No medical documentation, provider certification, or court order is required — the health-care provider certification requirement was removed in August 2021, and the X option has been available since January 1, 2020 under HB 669. The fee for the marker change is $3. Minors can also select X with parental consent.
new-hampshire.marker_overview: New Hampshire splits the rules by document: a driver's license or state ID can be changed to F, M, or X by self-identification with no medical documentation or court order, but a birth certificate requires a court order for a 'sex change' under RSA 5-C:87, and X is not recognized on birth certificates. The license rules have survived recent repeal attempts — 2026 bills to remove the X marker (HB 1165) and to strip gender identity from nondiscrimination law (HB 1564) did not become law.
new-hampshire.surgery_required: No — no surgery, medical procedure, or doctor's letter is required for either document; the birth-certificate court order does not require proof of surgery, and the license change is by self-identification alone.

new-jersey.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Health, Office of Vital Statistics and Registry
new-jersey.birth_certificate: Submit the Request Form and Attestation to Amend Sex Designation on a Birth Certificate (REG-L2 for adults, REG-L3 for a minor's parent or guardian) to the New Jersey Department of Health, Office of Vital Statistics and Registry, Records Modification Unit, by mail or through the office's online system, selecting Female, Male, or Undesignated/Non-binary and attesting under penalty of perjury that the change conforms your legal gender to your gender identity and is not for a fraudulent purpose. Include a copy of your birth certificate or current government ID; a certified copy of a name-change court order is only needed if you are also changing your name. Fee: $2 to process the change, plus $25 for the first certified copy of the amended certificate and $2 for each additional copy. The amended certificate is not marked as amended and the original is placed under seal.
new-jersey.court_order_required: No — no court order is required to change the gender marker on either a birth certificate or a driver's license; a court order is needed only if you are also changing your legal name, and New Jersey courts can issue a gender-declaration order for residents born in states that do require one.
new-jersey.drivers_license: Complete the Declaration of Gender Designation Change form and bring it in person to any New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) Licensing Center, surrendering your current license or ID. You may indicate M, F, or X (non-binary/unspecified) by self-attestation — no medical documentation or doctor's signature is needed. Fee: $11 for the duplicate card.
new-jersey.marker_overview: New Jersey lets you change the gender marker on both a birth certificate and a driver's license or state ID by self-attestation, with Female, Male, or Undesignated/Non-binary (X on licenses) available on both. No medical documentation, doctor's signature, or surgery is required for either document, under the 2018 Babs Siperstein Law (N.J.S.A. 26:8-40.12, effective February 1, 2019), which ended the old surgery-proof requirement. A court order is needed only if you are also changing your legal name.
new-jersey.surgery_required: No — no surgery, medical procedure, or doctor's letter is required for either document; the 2018 Babs Siperstein Law expressly removed the prior requirement of proof of gender reassignment surgery.
